facts.text: Angle Inlet sits at the northernmost point of the contiguous United States, a pene‑exclave of Minnesota separated by Lake of the Woods.
The community’s post office proudly displays a sign declaring it the “Most Northerly P.O. in Contiguous U.S.” and it also houses Minnesota’s last one‑room schoolhouse.
Travelers leaving Angle Inlet must first notify Canadian authorities before re‑entering Canada, then report again to the U.S. upon return.
The area was once home to a French‑Canadian fort staffed by about 40 voyageurs, abandoned around 1756 during the French and Indian War.
Angle Inlet’s isolation means it is only reachable by paved road from Manitoba, Canada, with a seasonal ice road linking it to the U.S. in winter.
The community’s landscape reflects post‑glacial deposition, featuring gentle rolls and a shoreline that floods seasonally, shaping its irregular coastal features.
